q: Why does BFS use a queue rather than a stack?
options: FIFO order processes nodes in the order they were discovered: level by level
why: A stack would dive deep first (that's DFS).

q: Why snapshot `len(q)` before processing a level?
options: Children are appended during the loop, so the length changes
To avoid errors on empty trees
why: Without the snapshot you'd mix the next level into this one.

q: Minimum depth of a tree with 100,000 nodes where one leaf sits at depth 2. Better approach?
options: BFS, stop at the first leaf
why: BFS reaches depth 2 almost immediately; DFS might explore the whole tree first.

q: Right side view: can a node from a LEFT subtree be visible?
options: Yes, when the right side has fewer levels
why: The view is the last node of each level, wherever it sits.

q: BFS queue size on a perfect binary tree of n nodes can reach…
why: The last level of a perfect tree holds about half the nodes.
